item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00040","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C06","C05","C23"],"selected_candidate_label":"C06","confidence":0.86,"relationship_type":"structural_functional_template","rationale":"C06 plausibly supplied a material structural template. Both memoranda reject legislation that would expand and extend an established federal aid program beyond its original justification; quantify the proposed expansion; argue that changed conditions require a different federal role; distinguish the rejected extension from a more carefully designed long-range or transitional policy; note that existing assistance will continue temporarily; and promise development of a better-targeted program. C05 has a similar veto-and-future-recommendations structure, but concerns compensation and lacks the especially close machinery of withdrawing from an established subsidy program. C23 likewise favors comprehensive, carefully designed legislation over an overbroad project-specific measure, but its operative sequence is less similar.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"the time has come for the federal Government to begin an orderly withdrawal from the airport grant program","parent_excerpt":"The interests of the domestic minerals industry will be better served by proceeding with the careful development of a long range minerals program than by approving a stopgap measure extending substantial Government aid","explanation":"Both pivot from extending an existing federal subsidy mechanism toward a deliberately redesigned long-term policy."},{"child_excerpt":"this bill does not provide for a transitional program. Rather, it sharply increases the level of the existing program","parent_excerpt":"H.R. 6373, in effect, would direct the expansion of these programs so as to require the Government to buy far greater quantities","explanation":"Each characterizes the rejected bill as an unjustified expansion of an existing program rather than an appropriate transition or reform."},{"child_excerpt":"At the next session of the Congress, the Administration will recommend a transitional program","parent_excerpt":"the Office of Minerals Mobilization has been established in the Department of the Interior to determine and recommend such a program","explanation":"Both replace the rejected extension with an executive effort to formulate a more suitable program."},{"child_excerpt":"The existing program continues through June 30, 1959, so no community will be hurt","parent_excerpt":"Meanwhile...the existing domestic minerals procurement program remains uncompleted, and sales by domestic miners to the Government will continue","explanation":"Both reassure affected beneficiaries that withholding approval will not abruptly terminate assistance because the existing program continues in the interim."}]}
